thread:
jamie: Heads up — canary shows ~18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate after the kernel selector change (cpu->gpu affinity tweak). heatmap: https://internal/heat/1754321987 :grimacing:
leigh: ugh. any idea if batching changed too or just key churn?
mike: quick question — are we sure it's key churn and not seq-length distribution shifting?
jamie: checked both. seq distribution stable. miss tails correlate with increased unique cache keys. profiler shows serialization calls spiking.
anya: ops-bot reports spike at 02:59 UTC when the canary rolled. deploy-bot: canary deployed 02:58:47 UTC to 10% traffic.
mike: could be serialization ordering. we changed the kernel path to use a C++ unordered_map for tool args, earlier python path used sorted dict.
jamie: exactly. old keyer did canonical JSON with sort_keys=True. new path now returns different ordering for tool/function call fields, so identical logical prompts generate different kv keys.
leigh: that's nasty but fixable. what about tokenizer/version pinning? did that change?
jamie: tokenizer id got implicit defaulting to latest in the new codepath; older cached entries were created with pinned tokenizer v2.0. Now new keys are tagged v2.1, so keys diverge.
mike: shortlist of fixes: (1) canonicalize tool args (sort), (2) include explicit tokenizer version in key, (3) consider dual-lookup fallback for a transition window.
jamie: agreed. quick PoC for canonical keyer (pseudo):
```
def make_key(prompt, tool_args, sys_prompt, tokenizer_id):
    normalized_prompt = normalize_whitespace(prompt)
    canonical_tool_args = json.dumps(tool_args, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"))
    payload = {"sys": normalize_whitespace(sys_prompt), "prompt": normalized_prompt, "tool": canonical_tool_args, "tok": tokenizer_id}
    return sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
```
mike: note the double json.dumps for tool args — we want stable string representation. also strip/control chars from sys prompts.
anya: operational concern — if we change the key schema customers with long-lived prefix caches may see misses until backfill. what's the warmup/backfill plan?
jamie: options: A) backfill proactively by replaying recent traffic to regenerate new keys on Dedicated pools; B) dual-lookup: check new key, if miss then check legacy key and populate new key on hit; C) short-term increase in cache capacity to absorb misses while we warm up.
leigh: dual-lookup seems safer with minimal customer impact. cost: extra lookup latency on misses. we can optimize path to only do legacy-lookup when new-key miss and when request marked as eligible for legacy-fallthrough.
mike: also add a signature version field in metadata so we can roll future key changes without ambiguity.
jamie: perf tradeoff: additional canonicalization CPU cost. but profiling shows serialization was cheap compared to the downstream miss cost. tradeoff is acceptable.
anya: ops: can we run an A/B where 5% traffic uses dual-lookup, 5% uses canonical-only, and rest is baseline? then measure hit-rate delta and p99 latency.
deploy-bot: rollout plan created: canary groups -> {A: baseline, B: dual-lookup, C: new-key-only} at 2%/2%/1% starting 04:30 UTC if approved.
mike: also add unit tests for tool-field ordering, and fuzz tests with reordered args.
leigh: will create an e2e perf job that replays 24h of production traces to estimate backfill time and cost.
jamie: action items:
- jamie: PR for canonical keyer + tokenizer pin (draft) by EOD
- mike: add dual-lookup logic + metrics (hit_source) by tomorrow
- leigh: snapshot replay job and cost estimate by EOD tomorrow
- anya: ops to hold canary at 10% until metric checks pass; alert if eviction rate > +15%
anya: tagging infra oncall for attention: @ops-oncall :bell:
mike: test note — also watch kernel selector path: ensure no other reorders (maps, sets) leak into serialization.
jamie: thanks — will post PR link and perf numbers once PoC runs. :thumbsup:
